title: Randomized sharer profiles for trust and closeness
rationale: In the source study, close ties (+3.0 points) and high trust (+5.7 points; low-trust cell n=817) were measured on real contacts and bundle correlated traits. Randomly assigning vignette sharers' closeness and trustworthiness tests whether these associations survive randomization. A 'would not share' option removes the forced-choice link.
contribution: Provides randomized estimates of sharer closeness and trustworthiness effects on sharing across true, false and fact-check content.
limitations: Vignette sharers are hypothetical and may differ from real contacts
Stated sharing likelihood may not match real behaviour; the click is only a subsample proxy
Trust is described rather than experienced
Single-post ratings differ from the source's paired forced choice
The compact instrument shows one profile per respondent; the full run randomizes per task

design.title: Randomized sharer profiles for trust and closeness
design.overview: US adults see 8 single posts. Each post is attributed to a vignette sharer whose closeness (close or distant) and trustworthiness (low, high; mid added in the full run) are randomly assigned, crossed with information type (true, misinformation, fact-check). Respondents give a 0-100 sharing likelihood or choose 'would not share'. A subsample makes a behavioural share-to-feed click.
design.hypothesis: Randomly assigned close and high-trust sharers raise sharing likelihood relative to distant and low-trust sharers (about 3 points), with effects possibly differing by information type.
design.primaryOutcome: Sharing likelihood (0-100), with 'would not share' analysed separately as a binary outcome.
design.comparison: Close vs distant; high vs low trust; main effects pooled over information type, with exploratory interactions with information type.
design.population: Quota-sampled US adults (age, gender, race, party)

questions.text: This survey asks how you would respond to social media posts. It takes about 10 minutes and is voluntary. Do you agree to participate?
Thank you for your time. The survey ends here.
You will see several posts. Each was shared with you by a fictional person we describe. Imagine the person is real.
The person who shared the next post is a close contact, someone you discuss important matters with. People describe them as very trustworthy. Post: {{ed:post_ch}}
How likely are you to share this post? Enter a number from 0 (not at all) to 100 (certainly).
Would you choose not to share this post at all?
The person who shared the next post is a close contact, someone you discuss important matters with. People describe them as not very trustworthy. Post: {{ed:post_cl}}
How likely are you to share this post? Enter a number from 0 (not at all) to 100 (certainly).
Would you choose not to share this post at all?
The person who shared the next post is a distant acquaintance you rarely interact with. People describe them as very trustworthy. Post: {{ed:post_dh}}
How likely are you to share this post? Enter a number from 0 (not at all) to 100 (certainly).
Would you choose not to share this post at all?
The person who shared the next post is a distant acquaintance you rarely interact with. People describe them as not very trustworthy. Post: {{ed:post_dl}}
How likely are you to share this post? Enter a number from 0 (not at all) to 100 (certainly).
Would you choose not to share this post at all?
Would you like to add the last post to a practice feed that we will show to other participants?
Thank you. The sharers were fictional and some posts were false or corrections. Please do not rely on any false claims you saw.

assumptions: Power: about 1500 respondents per arm to detect 0.03 at 80% power (observed close-tie 0.030, trust-high 0.057; source H2 MDE 0.0258 at n 6709/5256), with SEs clustered by respondent and task.

Each respondent completes 8 tasks; the instrument shows one example task and the platform repeats it with new posts, information type randomized per task (true, misinformation, fact-check). The mid-trust level is added in the full factorial.
Quota-sampled US adults via an online panel; the click is asked of a random subsample.
The 0-100 likelihood is entered as a number in a text-entry field.
Within each respondent, sharer profile is fixed in the compact example; the full run randomizes per task.
unresolved: Actual post images and the headline pool must be supplied by the research team.
Compensation, IRB number and panel vendor are to be set by the research team.
